Things 71–80: I/O, CAP, Lineage, and Scalability

第 8 章（共 10 章）：I/O、CAP、血缘与可扩展性（第 71–80 篇）

71. The Hidden Cost of Data Input/Output数据输入/输出的隐性成本

Lohit VijayaRenu

洛希特·维贾亚雷努

While data engineers are exposed to libraries and helper functions to read and write data, knowing certain details about the process of reading and writing operations helps you optimize your applications. Understanding and having the ability to configure various options can help with many data-intensive applications, especially at scale. The following are a few hidden details associated with data input/output (I/O).

数据工程师虽然天天用读写数据的库和辅助函数，但了解读写操作过程中的某些细节，能帮你优化应用。理解并能配置各种选项，对许多数据密集型应用有帮助，尤其是在大规模时。下面是与数据输入/输出（I/O）相关的几个隐藏细节。

Data Compression数据压缩

While everyone agrees that compressed data can save disk space and reduce the cost of network transfer, you can choose from a plethora of compression algorithms for your data. You should always consider the compression speed versus compression ratio while choosing an algorithm. This applies to compression as well as decompression operations. For example, if the data is already heavy, choosing a faster decompression algorithm while sacrificing more resources for slower compression pays off.

虽然大家都同意压缩数据能省磁盘空间、降低网络传输成本，但你可以从一大堆压缩算法中选。选算法时一定要权衡压缩速度与压缩率。这对压缩和解压缩操作都适用。例如，如果数据本身已经很大，选一个更快的解压算法、在压缩上牺牲更多资源换慢速，是划算的。

Data Format数据格式

While most unstructured data is a collection of records, that might not be the best format for certain types of data access. For example, a record that has multiple nested fields, of which only a few are accessed frequently, is best stored in a columnar data format instead of a record format. You should consider using different levels of nesting versus flattening columns for efficient writing as well as data-retrieval operations. This also pays off in cost savings for your data storage.

虽然大多数非结构化数据是记录的集合，但对某些数据访问类型来说，这未必是最佳格式。例如，一条记录有多个嵌套字段、其中只有少数被频繁访问，最好用列式数据格式而不是记录格式存储。你应该权衡不同嵌套层级与扁平化列，以同时高效地写入和检索数据。这还能帮你省下数据存储成本。

Data Serialization数据序列化

Most data is serialized into records using various formats. Structured data that is represented in various data formats should be serialized during writing and then deserialized every time it is read back. This process is usually hidden from users, but choosing efficient serialization/deserialization options (in a serde library) will greatly improve overall application performance at scale.

大多数数据用各种格式序列化成记录。以各种数据格式表示的结构化数据，在写入时应被序列化，每次读回时再反序列化。这个过程通常对用户隐藏，但在 serde 库中选择高效的序列化/反序列化选项，会在大规模时大幅改善应用整体性能。

— p.169 —

While there are many more aspects of I/O performance, knowing some of these details can help improve the overall performance of applications. Data engineers should take time to understand them and profile their applications to break down hidden costs associated with I/O.

虽然 I/O 性能还有许多其他方面，但了解其中一些细节就能帮你改善应用整体性能。数据工程师应花时间理解它们，并对应用做剖析，拆解与 I/O 相关的隐性成本。

— p.170 —

72. The Holy War Between Proprietary and Open Source Is a Lie专有与开源之间的圣战是个谎言

Paige Roberts (Vertica Open Source Relations Manager)

佩奇·罗伯茨（Vertica 开源关系经理）

You don't have to choose sides in some imaginary holy war. Open source software can be great, so can proprietary software. The one metric to rule them all is: use what works best.

你不必在某场想象中的圣战里选边站。开源软件可以很好，专有软件也可以很好。唯一统治一切的指标是：用效果最好的。

A lot of data engineers and architects feel like they have to pick a side between open source software and proprietary. You don't. Seriously, there are no sides.

许多数据工程师和架构师觉得必须在开源软件和专有软件之间选边。你不必。说真的，没有什么边。

The same engineers who write proprietary code often also write open source code. But which side of the line is open core software on? What about proprietary software with open source components, or proprietary software that allows you to embed or integrate open source components? Why the heck are you worrying about this? The only thing a data engineer should worry about is how to get a project into production most efficiently.

写专有代码的工程师常常也写开源代码。但 open core 软件站在哪一边？带开源组件的专有软件呢？允许你嵌入或集成开源组件的专有软件呢？你到底为什么要操心这个？数据工程师唯一该操心的是：如何最高效地把项目弄上生产。

The main difference between an open source and a proprietary offering is that one was made by developers for developers, and the other was made by developers for customers. Customers tend to want greater ease of use and dependability. They'll settle for less control if it means they can get jobs into production faster, won't have to hire a specialist, and can rely on the solution. Developers want more power and control knobs. They'll settle for less ease of use and dependability if it means they get greater flexibility.

开源产品和专有产品的主要区别在于：一个是开发者为开发者做的，另一个是开发者为客户做的。客户往往想要更好用、更可靠。如果这意味着他们能更快把工作弄上生产、不必雇专家、可以依赖这个解决方案，他们会接受更少的控制。开发者想要更多力量和调节旋钮。如果这意味着更大的灵活性，他们会接受更差的易用性和可靠性。

Power, flexibility, ease of use, speed to production, and dependability are all important. When you make your choice, think about the skills available to you, now and in the foreseeable future. Weigh the advantages of speed to production versus flexibility during the development stage. Think about the burden of ongoing maintenance, and your project's tolerance for occasional downtime. Consider whether any of those adjustment knobs are essential for your project.

力量、灵活性、易用性、上线速度、可靠性都重要。做选择时，想想你现在和可预见未来拥有的技能。权衡上线速度与开发阶段灵活性。想想持续运维的负担、以及你的项目对偶尔停机的容忍度。想想那些调节旋钮对你的项目是否必不可少。

— p.171 —

Sometimes what works best will be open source software; other times, it will be proprietary. Sometimes building something from scratch is necessary, although that's likely to be the most expensive in time and expertise. Regardless of what you choose this time, nothing stops you from making an entirely different choice for the next job.

有时效果最好的是开源软件；有时是专有软件。有时从零构建是必要的，尽管那在时间和专业上可能最昂贵。无论你这次选什么，都不妨碍你下一份工作做完全不同的选择。

Also, consider integration. Best of breed makes a lot of sense, but if you spend half your time trying to get disparate software products to talk to each other, that isn't a win. Integration capability isn't an open source versus proprietary thing, either. Getting software built by one team to talk to software built by another is always a challenge. Even proprietary software from one vendor sometimes was built by multiple teams, and shoved together without much thought to making it integrate.

还要考虑集成。最佳组合（best of breed）听起来很合理，但如果你花一半时间让不同软件互相通话，那不是胜利。集成能力也不是开源对专有 的事。让一个团队写的软件和另一个团队写的软件对话，永远是个挑战。即使是同一个厂商的专有软件，有时也是多个团队写的、凑在一起、没怎么考虑让它们集成。

Choose software that works and plays well with others, particularly other software that you already know your project requires. And look at how much of the job a single application can accomplish. If one thing can do multiple parts of your task, that will reduce your integration burden.

选择好用、也能和其他软件友好协作的软件，尤其是你的项目已经知道需要的其他软件。看看单个应用能完成任务的多大比例。如果一个东西能做你任务的多个部分，就会减轻你的集成负担。

Judge by your needs, your available resources, and what will give your project the best ROI.

根据你的需求、可用资源、以及什么能给项目最佳 ROI 来判断。

— p.172 —

73. The Implications of the CAP TheoremCAP 定理的影响

Paul Doran

保罗·多兰

The CAP theorem forces us to compromise between consistency, availability, and partition tolerance in distributed data systems:

CAP 定理迫使我们在分布式数据系统中，在一致性、可用性和分区容忍之间做权衡：

  • Consistency means all clients see the same response to a query.
    一致性（Consistency）意味着所有客户端看到同一查询的相同响应。
  • Availability means every query from a client gets a response.
    可用性（Availability）意味着客户端的每个查询都得到响应。
  • Partition tolerance means the system works if the system loses messages.
    分区容忍（Partition tolerance）意味着系统丢消息时仍能工作。

As data engineers, we must accept that distributed data systems will have partitions, so we need to understand the compromise between consistency and availability. Constructing robust data pipelines requires us to understand what could go wrong. By definition, a data pipeline needs to move data from one place to another.

作为数据工程师，我们必须接受分布式数据系统会有分区，因此需要理解一致性和可用性之间的权衡。构建健壮的数据管道要求我们理解哪里可能出问题。按定义，数据管道需要把数据从一个地方搬到另一个地方。

Here are three things to note about the CAP theorem's impact on system design:

关于 CAP 定理对系统设计的影响，有三点需要注意：

  • Attempting to classify data systems as being either CP or AP is futile. The classification could depend on the operation or the configuration. The system might not meet the theorem's definitions of consistency and availability.
    试图把数据系统归类为 CP 或 AP 是徒劳的。这个分类可能取决于操作或配置。系统可能根本不满足定理对一致性和可用性的定义。
  • While the CAP theorem seems limiting in practice, it cuts off only a tiny part of the design space. It disallows those systems that have perfect availability and consistency in the presence of network partitions.
    虽然 CAP 定理在实践中看似限制颇多，但它只切掉了设计空间的一小部分。它禁止的是那种在网络分区时仍同时拥有完美可用性和一致性的系统。
  • The only fault considered is a network partition. We know from practice that we need to think about many more failure modes in real-world systems.
    它考虑的唯一故障是网络分区。我们从实践中知道，现实世界系统需要考虑多得多的故障模式。

Having said that, the CAP theorem forces us to think about data system design. It forces us to ask questions about the systems we build and use. It forces us to ensure that we are meeting the needed requirements and expectations.

话虽如此，CAP 定理迫使我们思考数据系统设计。它迫使我们对自己构建和使用的系统提出问题。它迫使我们确保满足所需的需求和预期。

— p.173 —

But the CAP theorem says nothing about what to do when things are running normally. The PACELC theorem builds on CAP and tells us that in the absence of partitions, the trade-off is between latency and consistency. If we are going to build and use highly available data systems, those systems will have to replicate data across nodes. A single node is a single point of failure. This data replication is at the heart of the trade-off; how long are we willing to wait for data to replicate? We could wait for it to replicate to all nodes before making it available to ensure consistency, or we could keep the data available and accept that some users might see out-of-date data.

但 CAP 定理对一切正常运行时该怎么做只字未提。PACELC 定理在 CAP 之上构建，告诉我们：在没有分区时，权衡在延迟和一致性之间。如果我们要构建和使用高可用数据系统，这些系统必须跨节点复制数据。单节点就是单点故障。这种数据复制是权衡的核心：我们愿意等多久让数据复制完？我们可以等它复制到所有节点再对外可用以保证一致性，也可以让数据保持可用、接受某些用户可能看到过时数据。

The data pipelines we build need to understand these choices. This is an important step toward building robust data pipelines. Extracting data from a database may require different choices than consuming data from a message queue.

我们构建的数据管道需要理解这些选择。这是走向健壮数据管道的重要一步。从数据库抽取数据，可能需要与从消息队列消费数据不同的选择。

The CAP theorem is an important result, but it is only a small part of the picture. It allows us to frame our thinking and understanding of the technologies we use, but it does not allow us to stop thinking about who our customers are and what they need.

CAP 定理是一个重要结果，但它只是图景的一小部分。它让我们能框定对所用技术的思考和理解，但它不让我们停止思考：我们的客户是谁、他们需要什么。

— p.174 —

74. The Importance of Data Lineage数据血缘的重要性

Julien Le Dem

朱利安·勒·戴姆

As a data engineer, you become a sort of collector of datasets coming from various sources. The challenge is that datasets don't just stay pinned on a board behind glass. They have to be maintained and updated in a timely manner. They have to be transformed and adapted to various use cases. They change form over time; all the layers built upon them have to be updated. As data pipelines pile up, complexity increases dramatically, and it becomes harder to keep things updated reliably in a timely manner. Observing data lineage in all the layers of transformation—from ingestion to machine learning, business intelligence, and data processing in general—provides a critical source of visibility. With this information, the engineer on call can understand what's happening and resolve problems quickly when a crisis happens.

作为数据工程师，你成了某种数据集收集者，数据集来自各种源。挑战在于数据集不会只钉在玻璃后面的板子上。它们必须被及时维护和更新。它们必须被转换、适配到各种用例。它们随时间变形；建在它们之上的所有层都必须更新。随着数据管道堆积，复杂度急剧上升，可靠、及时地保持更新变得越来越难。在所有转换层观察数据血缘——从接入到机器学习、商业智能、一般数据处理——提供了关键的可见性来源。有了这些信息，值班工程师能理解发生了什么，在危机发生时快速解决问题。

Lineage provides the understanding of how a dataset was derived from another one. Operational lineage goes one step beyond by tracing how and when that transformation happened. It captures information such as:

血缘提供了一个数据集如何从另一个数据集派生的理解。运维血缘更进一步，追踪这个转换是如何、何时发生的。它捕获以下信息：

  • The version of the input that was consumed
    被消费的输入版本
  • The subset of the data that was read
    被读取的数据子集
  • The version of the code doing the transformation
    执行转换的代码版本
  • The output's definition and how each column was derived from the input
    输出的定义、以及每列如何从输入派生
  • The time it took to complete and whether it was successful
    完成耗时、是否成功
  • The version of the output that was produced
    所产出输出的版本
  • The shape of the output data (schema, row count, distribution, ...)
    输出数据的形态（schema、行数、分布……）

Tracking operational lineage changes over time provides the critical information needed to quickly answer many questions arising when data-related problems occur:

随时间跟踪运维血缘变化，提供了快速回答数据相关问题出现时的许多问题所需的关键信息：

— p.175 —
  • My transformation is failing. Did anything change upstream? Did the shape of the input data change? Where did this change originate? Did someone change the logic of the transformation producing it?
    我的转换在失败。上游有什么变化吗？输入数据的形态变了吗？这个变化从哪里来？有人改了产生它的转换逻辑吗？
  • My dataset is late. Where is the bottleneck upstream? How can this bottleneck be explained? Has it become slower recently? If yes, what has changed about its definition and its input?
    我的数据集晚了。上游瓶颈在哪里？怎么解释这个瓶颈？它最近变慢了吗？如果是，它的定义和输入有什么变化？
  • My dataset is incorrect. What changed in the shape of the data? Where upstream did the distribution of this column start drifting? What change in transformation logic is correlated with the change of data shape?
    我的数据集不对。数据形态哪里变了？这一列的分布从上游哪里开始漂移？转换逻辑的什么变化与数据形态变化相关？

OpenLineage is the open source project standardizing lineage and metadata collection across the data ecosystem. With a data-collection platform in place, a data engineer can move fast and fix things fast. They can quickly perform impact analysis to prevent new changes from breaking things by answering such questions as: Will this schema change break downstream consumers? Who should be informed about this semantic change? Can we deprecate this dataset?

OpenLineage 是在整个数据生态中标准化血缘和元数据采集的开源项目。有了数据采集平台，数据工程师可以快速行动、快速修复。他们可以快速做影响分析，通过回答这些问题来防止新变更破坏东西：这个 schema 变更会搞坏下游消费方吗？谁应该被告知这个语义变更？我们能弃用这个数据集吗？

Lineage is also the basis of many other data-related needs:

血缘也是许多其他数据相关需求的基础：

  • Privacy. Where is my users' private data consumed? Is it used according to user consent?
    隐私。我的用户隐私数据在哪里被消费？是否按用户同意使用？
  • Discovery. What datasets exist, and how are they consumed? How is this dataset derived from others? Who owns it?
    发现。有哪些数据集？它们如何被消费？这个数据集如何从其他派生？谁拥有它？
  • Compliance. Can I prove that my reporting is correctly derived from my input data?
    合规。我能证明我的报表是从输入数据正确派生的吗？
  • Governance. Am I using the data correctly?
    治理。我在正确使用数据吗？

As the number of datasets and jobs grows within an organization, these questions quickly become impossible to answer without collecting data-lineage metadata. This knowledge is the strong foundation that allows data to be manageable at scale.

随着组织内数据集和作业数量增长，如果不采集数据血缘元数据，这些问题很快就无法回答。这种知识是让数据在大规模下可管理的坚实基础。

— p.176 —

75. The Many Meanings of Missingness缺失的多种含义

Emily Riederer

艾米丽·里德勒

Missing data is possibly one of the best-explored topics in traditional data management; preventing null values is the textbook example for a database constraint, and detecting nulls is the same for data validation. However, missing data should not simply be dodged. By considering the many meanings of missing, data engineers can make more-thoughtful decisions about how to encode and communicate this missingness to end users.

缺失数据可能是传统数据管理中被研究得最透的课题之一；防止空值是数据库约束的教科书示例，检测空值是数据校验的同等待遇。然而，缺失数据不应简单地被躲开。通过思考“缺失”的多种含义，数据工程师可以更周到地决定如何编码、如何把这种缺失传达给终端用户。

It's tempting to think of missingness as a binary: the data exists or does not. However, this view ignores the potentially informative nature of nulls. Missingness can arise in numerous ways, each with its own analytical challenges. For example, a variable for an observation might appear to be missing because of the following:

人很容易把缺失想成二元：数据存在或不存在。然而这个观点忽略了空值可能具有的信息量。缺失可以以多种方式出现，每种都有自己的分析挑战。例如，一个观测的变量可能因为以下原因看似缺失：

  • A true value for that variable exists, but it was loaded incorrectly.
    该变量的真实值存在，但加载错误。
  • A true value for that variable exists, but it was intentionally uncollected.
    该变量的真实值存在，但被故意不采集。
  • A true value for that variable exists, but it is unknown.
    该变量的真实值存在，但未知。
  • No relevant value exists for that variable.
    该变量不存在相关值。
  • The relevant value for that variable is null.
    该变量的相关值就是 null。

To illustrate, consider a dataset of users registering for an online ecommerce platform:

举例来说，考虑一个在线电商平台注册用户的数据集：

  • A mismatch in account ID formats across tables, or arithmetic performed using a null and a non-null field, could introduce null values.
    跨表账户 ID 格式不匹配、或用 null 与非 null 字段做算术，可能引入空值。
  • A random sample of users is invited to complete a survey, and responses are recorded for only that sample.
    随机抽样的用户被邀请填问卷，只有该样本记录了回答。
  • Users might be optionally asked for their birthdate. Every user has a birthdate, but only some are recorded.
    用户可能被可选地询问出生日期。每个用户都有出生日期，但只有部分被记录。
  • We might record whether mobile users registered from an Android or iPhone device, but there is no relevant value for users who registered from a Windows phone.
    我们可能记录移动用户是从 Android 还是 iPhone 注册的，但从 Windows phone 注册的用户没有相关值。
  • Often retailers want to attribute user traffic to the referring source URL from which a user came. However, for users who type in the URL directly, the true value of the referring site is null.
    零售商常常想把用户流量归因到用户来源 URL。然而对于直接输入 URL 的用户，来源站点的真实值就是 null。
— p.177 —

For data analysts and scientists consuming your data, this distinction is more than semantics. Nulls that represent an issue loading data raise concerns about overall data quality; nulls from random sampling can possibly be safely ignored; nulls that represent aspects of user feedback could themselves become features in a model or analysis. (To continue one of the preceding examples, perhaps a user's unwillingness to share their birthdate could be a predictor of churn.)

对于消费你数据的数据分析师和科学家，这种区分不止是语义。代表加载问题的空值会引发对整体数据质量的担忧；来自随机抽样的空值可能可以安全忽略；代表用户反馈方面的空值本身可能成为模型或分析的特征。（接着前面的例子：也许用户不愿透露出生日期，本身就是流失的预测因子。）

As an engineer, you are closer to the generating system and may have more ability and insight to identify the root cause of missingness and pass this along. You can preserve far more information from the data-generating process by identifying the cause of missingness and thinking critically about how to represent this in the data. Should missingness be implicit (for example, no row in a table or field in JSON) or explicit? Should the value be null, a sentinel (e.g., a birthdate of 1900-01-01 or income of 999999999), or a shadow field (e.g., null in the main field with another field categorizing the missingness)? There's no one-size-fits-all solution, but recognizing and specifically designing for such nuance embeds value in an otherwise void of information.

作为工程师，你离产生数据的系统更近，可能更有能力和洞见识别缺失的根因并把它传下去。通过识别缺失原因、批判性地思考如何在数据中表示它，你可以从数据产生过程中保留多得多的信息。缺失应该是隐式的（例如表中没行、JSON 中没字段）还是显式的？值应该是 null、一个哨兵（例如出生日期 1900-01-01、收入 999999999），还是一个影子字段（例如主字段是 null、另一个字段对缺失分类）？没有放之四海皆准的方案，但识别这种细微差别并专门为之设计，会在原本信息真空中嵌入价值。

— p.178 —

76. The Six Words That Will Destroy Your Career会毁掉你职业生涯的六个字

Bartosz Mikulski

巴托什·米库尔斯基

Six words can destroy your credibility and jeopardize your career: "This number does not look correct." When you hear those words, it is already too late. People don't trust you anymore. They are suspicious about everything you have done so far. Suddenly, you become a person who makes mistakes—the person who has probably been feeding us false data for years.

六个字可以摧毁你的信誉、危及你的职业生涯：“这个数字看起来不对。”当你听到这六个字时，已经太晚了。人们不再信任你。他们对你到目前为止做的一切都起疑。突然之间，你成了一个会犯错的人——那个可能多年来一直在喂给我们假数据的人。

Is there anything to worry about? What if the timing was terrible, and somebody recently made a wrong decision that caused the company to lose tons of money? Suddenly, every decision becomes data driven. Even the people who ignored the data for years claim that they were making data-driven decisions. The problem is that the data is incorrect.

有什么好担心的？如果时机刚好很糟——最近有人做了一个错误决定导致公司亏了一大笔钱——怎么办？突然之间，每个决策都变成了数据驱动。就连那些多年来无视数据的人也声称自己在做数据驱动决策。问题是：数据是错的。

The data is wrong because you have made a mistake! Congratulations! You've been promoted to a scapegoat! Everybody in the company is going to know your name. You have just become the Excuse of the Year.

数据错了，因为你犯了错！恭喜！你被提拔为替罪羊！公司里每个人都会知道你的名字。你刚刚成为年度借口。

Do you want that? No? What are you doing to avoid such a situation? How often are "hope" and "luck" a vital part of the data pipeline? We hope that the data format does not change. If we get lucky, the files get uploaded before we generate the report for the CEO. Of course, if it fails, we have a person who restarts it manually, and nobody notices the problem.

你想要这样吗？不想？那你在做什么来避免这种局面？“希望”和“运气”多久成为数据管道的关键部分一次？我们希望数据格式不变。如果运气好，文件会在我们给 CEO 生成报告之前上传完。当然，如果失败，我们有一个人手动重启，没人注意到问题。

Data engineering is no different from other branches of software development. We can apply functional programming principles and turn our pipelines into something that resembles a function. Sure, the input is huge, and the function runs for a few hours, but for any given input, there is only one correct output, and we can write tests to ensure that we get what we expect.

数据工程与软件开发的其他分支没什么不同。我们可以应用函数式编程原则，把管道变成某种类似函数的东西。当然，输入巨大，函数跑几小时，但对任何给定输入，只有一个正确输出，我们可以写测试来确保得到预期结果。

Does it seem trivial and obvious? So why are there so many data pipelines without a single line of test code?

这看起来是不是太琐碎、太显而易见？那为什么有那么多数据管道一行测试代码都没有？

The other best practices we can copy come from site reliability engineering (SRE) teams. These include relentless automation and monitoring. Manual configuration leads to systems that are fragile, unpredictable, and cannot be fixed. You never know what is going to happen when you change something. You can't create a test environment because you don't even know the current state of the production system. It's a nightmare.

我们可以照搬的其他最佳实践来自站点可靠性工程（SRE）团队。包括无情的自动化和监控。手工配置导致系统脆弱、不可预测、无法修复。你永远不知道改东西时会发生什么。你建不了测试环境，因为你连生产系统的当前状态都不知道。这是噩梦。

— p.179 —

Similarly, the lack of monitoring will make you wake up screaming at night. Do you know whether your pipeline processes all of the data? What if it drops 3% and nobody knows about it? We should gather instrumentation metrics about the code we run and about the data we process. You would be surprised by the number of issues you can detect by comparing the histograms of input values and the pipeline output.

同样，缺乏监控会让你夜里惊醒尖叫。你知道你的管道处理了所有数据吗？如果它丢了 3% 而没人知道呢？我们应该为运行的代码、处理的数据采集仪表指标。通过比较输入值直方图和管道输出直方图，你能发现的问题数量会让你惊讶。

Of course, all of that must be automated as a part of the pipeline, and the whole process must fail if any validation detects incorrect values. Otherwise, it becomes an expensive toy that nobody uses and nobody cares about.

当然，所有这些必须作为管道的一部分自动化，如果任何校验检测到不正确值，整个流程必须失败。否则，它就变成一个没人用、也没人在乎的昂贵玩具。

— p.180 —

77. The Three Invaluable Benefits of Open Source for Testing Data Quality开源在数据质量测试上的三大无价好处

Tom Baeyens

汤姆·巴延斯

As a software engineer turned data engineer, I can attest to the importance of data in organizations today. I can also attest to the fact that the software engineering principles of writing unit tests and monitoring applications should be applied to data. However, even though people know they should test data, they often don't have the good practices or knowledge to approach it. Enter open source. In this chapter, I explore three areas in which open source software presents data-testing benefits: for the data engineer, for the enterprise as a whole, and for the tools developers create and use.

作为一个从软件工程师转行的数据工程师，我可以证明今天组织中数据的重要性。我也可以证明：写单元测试、监控应用的软件工程原则应该应用到数据上。然而即使人们知道应该测试数据，他们常常没有好实践或知识来做。开源登场。本章探讨开源软件在数据测试上呈现好处的三个领域：对数据工程师、对整个企业、对开发者创建和使用的工具。

Open source tools are developed by engineers, for engineers; if you're looking to start working with a data-testing tool that will naturally fit into your workflows, you have to start with open source. Open source software can also be embedded into data-engineering pipelines with ease: unencumbered by licensing restrictions or hidden costs, data engineers can be assured that open source tools will get to work quickly and easily.

开源工具是工程师为工程师开发的；如果你想开始使用一个自然融入你工作流的数据测试工具，必须从开源开始。开源软件还能轻松嵌入数据工程管道：不受许可限制或隐性成本束缚，数据工程师可以放心开源工具会快速轻松地开工。

For the enterprise, open source options have become a great way of getting started with data-quality initiatives. Implementing basic data testing and achieving better data quality in just a few days helps build the business case and starts uncovering data issues, helping avoid the pain of finding them too late. Open source projects allow for a frictionless approach to getting started and realizing results quickly. This enables far greater adoption by organizations and individuals. As a result, everyone can get closer to the data, and data teams can deliver high-quality, reliable insights with high velocity.

对企业而言，开源选项已成为启动数据质量举措的好方法。几天内实现基础数据测试、达到更好数据质量，有助于构建业务案例、开始暴露数据问题，帮助避免太晚发现问题的痛苦。开源项目让启动无摩擦、快速见到结果。这让组织和个人的采用率高得多。结果是：每个人都能离数据更近，数据团队能以高速度交付高质量、可靠的洞见。

Combining open source software with a cloud-based platform gives everyone the tools they need, in the way they like them, to get to work. Data quality is a team sport, and combining open source with the cloud provides an integrated and collaborative approach that gives modern data teams what they need to create transparency and trust in the data. To me, best-practice open source is to allow a common library that supports everything from tool development to common enterprise solutions, all readily accessible to the entire organization.

把开源软件与云平台结合，按每个人喜欢的方式，给他们开工所需的工具。数据质量是团队运动，把开源与云结合，提供了一种集成协作的方式，给现代数据团队创造数据透明度和信任所需的东西。对我而言，最佳实践的开源是允许一个公共库，支持从工具开发到通用企业方案的一切，整个组织都可随时访问。

— p.181 —

And really, it's that ability to engage and innovate that gets to the heart of the biggest opportunity that open source software brings to data testing. They say it takes a village to raise a child, but the same could equally be said of creating good-quality data. Open source development is boosted in both speed and creativity through community engagement, coding, and testing. Whereas a commercial data-testing product may have a small team looking at it, open source projects benefit from whole communities of dedicated data analysts and engineers.

说真的，正是那种参与和创新的能力，触及了开源软件给数据测试带来的最大机会的核心。人们说养一个孩子需要一个村庄，但创造高质量数据同样如此。通过社区参与、编码和测试，开源开发在速度和创造力两方面都被提升。商业数据测试产品可能只有一个小团队在看，开源项目则受益于整个社区敬业的数据分析师和工程师。

Open source software is opening up better data testing to those both within and outside the professional developer community. It's free, inclusive, built for purpose, and open to community-driven innovation—three invaluable benefits to improve data quality across all sectors.

开源软件正在向专业开发者社区内外的人开放更好的数据测试。它免费、包容、为目的而建、对社区驱动的创新开放——这三个无价好处，将改善所有行业的数据质量。

— p.182 —

78. The Three Rs of Data Engineering数据工程的三个 R

Tobias Macey

托比亚斯·梅西

In school we are told that the three Rs we need to know are reading, writing, and arithmetic. (I never did understand that, since only one of those words starts with R.) But once you grow up and get a job as a data engineer, you'll learn that there really are three Rs that you need to know, and in this case, they all actually start with that letter!

在学校里我们被告知，需要知道的三个 R 是阅读、写作和算术（reading、writing、arithmetic）。（我一直没搞懂，因为这三个词里只有一个以 R 开头。）但等你长大、做了数据工程师，你会发现真的有三个 R 需要知道，而且这次三个词真的都以那个字母开头！

Reliability可靠性（Reliability）

At the end of the day, the most important characteristic of your data is that it needs to be reliable. All the fancy machine learning and sophisticated algorithms in the world won't do you any good if you are feeding them messy and inconsistent data. Rather than the healthy, beautiful, and valuable systems that you know they could be, they will grow up to be hideous monsters that will consume your time and ambition.

归根结底，你数据最重要的特征是它必须可靠。如果你喂给它们乱糟糟、不一致的数据，世界上所有酷炫的机器学习和精密算法都对你没用。它们不会成为你所知道的那种健康、美丽、有价值的系统，而是长成狰狞的怪物，吞噬你的时间和抱负。

Reliability can mean a lot of things, but in this context we are talking about characteristics of your data that contribute to a high degree of confidence that the analyses you are performing can be assumed correct. Some of the elements of a data platform that is reliable are as follows:

可靠性可以指很多东西，但这里我们说的是你数据的那些特征——让你有高度信心认为你正在做的分析可以被假定为正确。一个可靠数据平台的一些要素如下：

  • Consistent and validated schemas. All records follow the same pattern and can be treated the same way by your analytical processes.
    一致且经过校验的 schema。所有记录遵循同一模式，可以被你的分析过程以同样方式处理。
  • High availability of your systems to ensure read and write operations succeed. This requires systems that provide redundancy (there's another R word) in the face of server and network failures that are inevitable.
    系统高可用，确保读写操作成功。这要求系统在不可避免的服务器和网络故障面前提供冗余（又一个 R 词）。
  • A well-defined and well-maintained repository of metadata that will provide the necessary context around what the data is, where it came from, and how it was produced. These questions will get asked at some point, so it's best to have the answers ahead of time.
    一个定义良好、维护良好的元数据仓库，提供关于数据是什么、从哪里来、如何产生的必要上下文。这些问题迟早会被问到，所以最好提前有答案。
  • Access control and auditability, to ensure that only the people and processes that are supposed to be able to modify the data are actually doing so.
    访问控制和可审计性，确保只有应该能修改数据的人和进程真的在做这件事。
— p.183 —

Reproducibility可复现性（Reproducibility）

Reproducibility is a critical competency when working with business-critical systems. If there is no way for another team member or business unit to independently verify and re-create your datasets and analytics, there is no way to be certain that the original results were valid. This also factors into the concept of reliability, because if you are able to consistently reproduce a given dataset, you can be fairly sure that it is reliable and can be trusted to be available.

在处理关键业务系统时，可复现性是一项关键能力。如果另一位团队成员或业务部门无法独立验证并重新创建你的数据集和分析，就无法确定原始结果是有效的。这也属于可靠性概念，因为如果你能一致地复现一个给定数据集，就可以相当确定它是可靠的、可以信任它是可用的。

Repeatability可重复性（Repeatability）

If all of your servers die, or the datacenter where your systems are running is destroyed or incapacitated by a natural disaster, you need a recovery plan. This is where the third R, repeatability, comes into play. It's all well and good to be able to build a Spark cluster or install a PostgreSQL database, but can you do it quickly and repeatedly? Having the configuration and procedures for repeating the installation or deployment of your data infrastructure feeds into the reproducibility of your data and the reliability of your analytics.

如果你所有服务器都挂了、或者你系统所在的数据中心被自然灾害摧毁或瘫痪，你需要一份恢复计划。第三个 R——可重复性——在这里登场。能建 Spark 集群、能装 PostgreSQL 数据库当然好，但你能快速且反复地做到吗？拥有重复安装或部署数据基础设施的配置和流程，会喂给你数据的可复现性和分析的可靠性。

Conclusion小结

Now that you have learned the three Rs of data engineering, you can be confident that the teams and systems depending on the output of your labor will be happy and successful. Just be sure to let them know how much work went into it, so that they can fully appreciate your dedication and perseverance.

既然你已经学了数据工程的三个 R，就可以相信依赖你劳动产出的团队和系统会快乐而成功。只是要让他们知道这里面花了多少功夫，好让他们充分欣赏你的奉献和毅力。

— p.184 —

79. The Two Types of Data Engineering and Data Engineers数据工程与数据工程师的两种类型

Jesse Anderson

杰西·安德森

There are two types of data engineering.¹ And there are two types of jobs with the title data engineer. This is especially confusing to organizations and individuals who are starting out learning about data engineering. This confusion leads to the failure of many teams' big data projects.

数据工程有两种类型。¹ 头衔为数据工程师的工作也有两种类型。这对刚开始学习数据工程的组织和个人尤其困惑。这种困惑导致许多团队的大数据项目失败。

Types of Data Engineering数据工程的类型

The first type of data engineering is SQL-focused. The work and primary storage of the data is in relational databases. All of the data processing is done with SQL or a SQL-based language. Sometimes this data processing is done with an ETL tool.

第一种数据工程是 SQL 导向的。工作和数据的主存储在关系数据库里。所有数据处理用 SQL 或 SQL 类语言完成。有时这种数据处理用 ETL 工具完成。

The second type of data engineering is big data–focused. The work and primary storage of the data is in big data technologies like Apache Hadoop, Cassandra, and HBase. All of the data processing is done in big data frameworks like MapReduce, Spark, and Flink. While SQL is used, the primary processing is done with programming languages like Java, Scala, and Python.

第二种数据工程是大数据导向的。工作和数据主存储在 Apache Hadoop、Cassandra、HBase 这类大数据技术里。所有数据处理在 MapReduce、Spark、Flink 这类大数据框架里完成。虽然也用 SQL，但主要处理用 Java、Scala、Python 这类编程语言完成。

Types of Data Engineers数据工程师的类型

The two types of data engineers closely match the types of data engineering. The first type of data engineer does their data processing with SQL. They may use an ETL tool. Sometimes their title is database administrator (DBA), SQL developer, or ETL developer. These engineers have little to no programming experience.

两种数据工程师与两种数据工程紧密对应。第一种数据工程师用 SQL 做数据处理。他们可能用 ETL 工具。有时他们的头衔是 DBA、SQL 开发者或 ETL 开发者。这些工程师几乎没有编程经验。

The second type of data engineer is a software engineer who specializes in big data. They have extensive programming skills and can write SQL queries too. The major difference is that these data engineers have the programming and SQL skills to choose between the two.

第二种数据工程师是专精大数据的软件工程师。他们有丰富的编程技能，也能写 SQL 查询。主要区别是：这些数据工程师同时具备编程和 SQL 技能，可以在两者之间选择。

Why These Differences Matter to You这些差异为什么对你重要

It's crucial that managers know the differences between these two types of data-engineering teams. Sometimes organizations will have a SQL-focused data-engineering team attempt a big data project. These sorts of efforts are rarely successful. For big data projects, you need the second type of data engineer and a data-engineering team that is big data–focused.

经理们了解这两种数据工程团队之间的差异至关重要。有时组织会让一个 SQL 导向的数据工程团队去尝试大数据项目。这种努力很少成功。大数据项目需要第二种数据工程师、以及大数据导向的数据工程团队。

For individuals, it's important to understand the required starting skills for big data. While there are SQL interfaces for big data, you need programming skills to get the data into a state that's queryable. For people who have never programmed before, this is a more difficult learning curve. I strongly recommend that SQL-focused people understand the amount of time it takes to learn how to program and the difficulty involved.

对个人来说，重要的是理解大数据所需的入门技能。虽然大数据有 SQL 接口，但你需要编程技能才能把数据弄到可查询的状态。对从没写过程序的人，这是一条更陡的学习曲线。我强烈建议 SQL 导向的人了解学编程要花多少时间、有多难。

Only by knowing and understanding these two definitions can you be successful with big data projects. You absolutely have to have the right people for the job.

只有了解并理解这两个定义，你才能在大数据项目上成功。你绝对必须有合适的人来做这份工作。

¹ A version of this chapter was originally published at jesse-anderson.com.

¹ 本章的一个版本最初发表于 jesse-anderson.com。

— p.185 —
— p.186 —

80. The Yin and Yang of Big Data Scalability大数据可扩展性的阴阳

Paul Brebner (Chief technology evangelist, Instaclustr.com)

保罗·布雷布纳（Instaclustr.com 首席技术布道师）

Modern big data technologies such as Apache Cassandra and Apache Kafka achieve massive scalability by using clusters of many nodes (servers) to deliver horizontal scalability. Horizontal scaling works by sharing workloads across all the nodes in a cluster by partitioning the data so that each node has a subset of the data, enabling throughput to be increased by simply adding more nodes, and replicating the data on more than one node for reliability, availability, and durability.

现代大数据技术如 Apache Cassandra 和 Apache Kafka，通过使用多节点（服务器）集群来交付水平扩展，从而实现海量可扩展性。水平扩展的工作方式是：把数据分区，让每个节点持有数据子集，跨集群所有节点共享工作负载，从而只需加节点就能提高吞吐；并把数据复制到多个节点以获得可靠性、可用性和持久性。

Being intrinsically scalable, Cassandra and Kafka are popular open source choices to run low-latency, high-throughput, and high-data-volume applications, which can be easily scaled out. We recently designed, tested, and scaled a demonstration anomaly detection application with Cassandra for the storage layer, Kafka for the streaming layer, and Kubernetes for application scaling. The following figure shows the anomaly detection pipeline's application design, clusters, and "knobs."

由于内在可扩展，Cassandra 和 Kafka 是运行低延迟、高吞吐、大数据量应用的流行开源选择，这些应用可以轻松向外扩展。我们最近设计、测试并扩展了一个演示用异常检测应用：存储层用 Cassandra、流处理层用 Kafka、应用扩缩用 Kubernetes。下图展示了异常检测管道的应用设计、集群和“旋钮”。

Scaling is also hard! To get close to linear scalability with increasing nodes, we had to tune multiple software resources to enable the hardware resources to be efficiently utilized. The untuned system achieved 7 billion checks/day, but tuning resulted in a 2.5 times improvement.

扩展也很难！为了在节点增加时接近线性扩展，我们必须调优多个软件资源，让硬件资源被高效利用。未调优的系统达到 70 亿次检查/天，但调优后提升了 2.5 倍。

The tuning "knobs" control hardware (cluster sizes) and software resources. By increasing the hardware resources (number of nodes in the Cassandra and Kafka clusters, and number of pods in the Kubernetes cluster), we eventually able to scale to 19 billion anomaly checks per day. This was an arbitrary number to stop at; there is no theoretical upper limit. It was achieved with a total of 574 CPU cores (Kafka: 72 cores/9 nodes; Kubernetes: 118 cores/100+ pods; Cassandra: 384 cores/48 nodes). So, scaling is easy just by adding hardware resources, but this isn't the complete story.

调优“旋钮”控制硬件（集群规模）和软件资源。通过增加硬件资源（Cassandra 和 Kafka 集群的节点数、Kubernetes 集群的 pod 数），我们最终扩展到每天 190 亿次异常检查。这只是一个随便停下的数字；理论上没有上限。它用总共 574 个 CPU 核实现（Kafka：72 核/9 节点；Kubernetes：118 核/100+ pod；Cassandra：384 核/48 节点）。所以，靠加硬件资源来扩展很容易，但故事并不完整。

— p.187 —

The most critical parameter was the number of Kafka partitions. In Kafka, partitions enable higher Kafka consumer concurrency, so we assumed that more was better. However, we found that increasing the number of partitions beyond a critical number significantly reduced the throughput of the Kafka cluster.

最关键的参数是 Kafka 分区数。在 Kafka 中，分区允许更高的消费者并发，所以我们以为越多越好。然而我们发现，把分区数增加到超过一个临界值后，Kafka 集群吞吐量显著下降。

Subsequent benchmarking revealed that Kafka cluster throughput is maximized with a "sweet spot" number of partitions, and throughput drops significantly—due to replication overhead—with too many partitions. So, counterintuitively, a critical part of the scaling process was optimizing the application pipeline to minimize the number of Kafka consumers and partitions to achieve the goal of maximum throughput.

后续基准测试揭示：Kafka 集群吞吐在某个“甜点”分区数下最大化，分区太多则因复制开销而显著下降。所以反直觉地，扩展过程的一个关键部分是优化应用管道，最小化 Kafka 消费者和分区数，以达到最大吞吐目标。

It's also important to make sure you have good data models for both Cassandra and Kafka. For Cassandra, use high-cardinality keys and bounded partitions. For Kafka, ensure that the key cardinality is much higher than the number of partitions (to prevent Knuth's parking problem), and don't start too many consumers at once (otherwise, you may get rebalancing storms).

还要确保 Cassandra 和 Kafka 都有好的数据模型。对 Cassandra，用高基数键和有界分区。对 Kafka，确保键基数远高于分区数（以防止 Knuth 停车问题），不要一次启动太多消费者（否则你可能遇到再均衡风暴）。
